### 1. What the caller expresses, and what the simulator will and will not do

Quoting the script: she "opens by saying her name, Delphine Marchetti, and that the desk should have her on 7030558214, then explains that she took out travel insurance in August for a tour she is taking to Japan in October with her husband and her sister, and that her hospital has since put her on its own corporate travel cover for the trip. Because of that she wants to cancel the policy and get back whatever she is owed, and she says so in those words."

- **Target object** — clear: the travel protection policy she took out in August for the October Japan tour. "She does not know her policy number or certificate number and says the desk will have to find them."
- **Timing** — now, on this call.
- **Boundary of the action** — she asks for two connected things and no more: cancel the policy, and return what she is owed. "She asks for no letter, no confirmation email and nothing else besides."
- **Mode of authorisation** — explicitly split, and she is emphatic: "She is content for the desk to put right anything on the policy that needs putting right at its end, and says so if the agent asks — 'if there's tidying up to do on your side, do it' — but **she says twice, unprompted, that she wants the cancellation itself confirmed by her**, not done quietly on her behalf, because it is her contract. When the agent explains what she is confirming and passes it to her, she goes through with it once and immediately."
- **Simulator discipline** — passive: "She keeps her paperwork close and reads from it only when asked." She names no tool and does not sequence the agent. "When a figure is put to her she accepts it without checking, saying she has no way of working it out herself."
- **Facts she volunteers or supplies on request:** DOB `1982-04-17`; card postal code `02139`; the operator's reference `WL-PKG-55218`; the tour "leaves on the tenth of October and comes back on the seventh of November"; "there are three adults on the booking and no children"; "she and her husband are the two named on the insurance, her sister having her own"; she has not travelled and has never claimed — "no to both, quite definitely"; and, asked whether the flights are part of the tour, "**she says no, they booked those separately in August and paid for them then**". On money: "a first amount left her card in August and thinks something small came back afterwards, but she would have to dig out the statement and would rather **the desk read it off the record**."

**Act now**, and the cancellation is hers to confirm. Grounds, all visible:

Clause 3 — "nothing is returned once any claim has been filed under the policy" — does not bite: `find_care_claims` returns "No care claims records match", and she says nothing has ever been claimed.
- *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* — "Only the policyholder may give up their own cover, and the cancellation is confirmed by the policyholder rather than performed on their behalf." Her own insistence matches.
- Whether she is inside or outside the free-look period is settled in §4c: 2026-08-30 → 2026-09-21 is 22 days against a TripGuard Plus free-look period of 14, so the mid-term terms apply. *Giving Up Cover…* clause 3: "Outside the free-look period the mid-term terms apply instead, and the two are never combined."
- Nothing here is uncovered ground; her reason (her employer's corporate cover) is not a condition of a mid-term surrender at all.

### 4. The scored parameters, in words, with inputs, intermediates and values

Three writes carry figures, and they must be worked in order (see §6), because each feeds the next.

#### 4a. Correct the declared trip cost — `corrected_trip_cost_usd`

Governing computation document: *Underwriting Basis for the Corrected Declaration on a Travel Protection Certificate* — "the declared trip cost is corrected to the prepaid cost of the journey the records show, and never above the plan's ceiling on the declared trip cost", assembled as: "The three deductions are taken together before the share is applied, and the figure at that point is never less than nothing; the share is then applied to it, and what has been prepaid for flights bought apart is added afterwards, outside the share. The corrected figure is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end."

Its own baseline quantities are: cost of the holiday = "The price the package was quoted at"; what counts as prepaid = "The whole of that cost, except the charges raised for optional components"; what has been returned = "Nothing"; what was settled other than in money = "Nothing"; the share = "The whole of that cost"; flights bought apart = "Nothing".

**Rules that decide an input by tiers, the tier this customer is on, and the returns that put her there:**

- **The cost of the holiday** — *The Cost of the Holiday Behind a Corrected Declaration*, reading 1: "The record stands confirmed **and** the ledger carries a final payment | The charges standing on that ledger: the deposits taken, the final payment and the charges raised for optional components, added together." The package `status` is **confirmed** and the ledger carries `bundle_final_payment_charge` 7600.00. → 1800.00 + 7600.00 + (620.00 + 480.00) = **10500.00**.
- **What counts as prepaid** — *What Counts as Prepaid on a Packaged Holiday*, reading 1: "Where the holiday's final payment has been taken **and** its ledger carries no penalty raised for a cancellation, the whole of that cost counts as prepaid." The final payment stands; the ledger carries no penalty row. → **10500.00**.
- **What has been returned** — *Money Returned by the Operator, Excluded From the Prepaid Cost*, reading 1: "The ledger carries money paid back to the traveller, **and** the record stands confirmed | The money paid back." `bundle_refund_payout` **−350.00** stands on a `confirmed` record. → **350.00**.
- **What was settled other than in money** — *Credit Settled Against a Packaged Holiday*, reading 1: "Where the holiday's ledger carries a future travel credit settled against it and its record shows no credit still standing open, what is taken out as settled other than in money is the credit settled." `bundle_credit_redeem` **−300.00** (voucher `WLFTC61204`) stands against it, and `credit_balance_usd` is **0.0**. → **300.00**.
- **The share of the party the certificate covers** — *The Certificate's Share of a Party's Prepaid Cost*, reading 1: "The party on the holiday is larger than the travellers named on the certificate, **and** the party is made up of adults only | The travellers named over the adults in the party." `party_adults` **3**, `party_children` **0**, certificate `insured_count` **2**. She confirms it in words: "there are three adults on the booking and no children … she and her husband are the two named on the insurance, her sister having her own". → **2/3**.
- **What has been prepaid for flights bought apart** — *Flights Bought Apart From the Holiday in a Corrected Declaration*, reading 1: "Where an air booking departing on the first date of the journey **stands ticketed** and the holiday's ledger **carries no flight component**, what has been prepaid for flights bought apart from the holiday is the money paid on that booking." Booking `496ba3da-…` departs **2026-10-10**, the journey's first date, and `status` is **ticketed**; `amount_paid_usd` **2240.0**. → **2240.00**. (On the ledger's `flight_upgrade` component charge, see §8 observation 1 — the document's own point of judgement, "because the flights are already inside the holiday's own cost", plus her statement that the flights were "booked separately in August", settle it: the fares are not inside the holiday's cost.)

**Assembly:** (10500.00 − 350.00 − 300.00) = 9850.00; × 2/3 = 6566.6666…; + 2240.00 = 8806.6666…; rounded once at the end = **8806.67**. The plan's ceiling on the declared trip cost is 20000 (*Travel Protection Plans — Acceptance Limits by Plan*, TripGuard Plus), so the cap does not bite.

Other parameters: `care_policy_id` `de27f4c9-0ba4-496a-93d8-0ead13e95e73`; `care_request_id` **`594e4876-610c-41e8-a851-d5edb7b43883`** ("the policy service request in which the underwriting desk recorded its approval of this correction").

#### 4b. Raise the premium re-rating — `rerating_amount_usd`

Governing computation document: *Rating Office Basis for a Re-Rating on a Travel Protection Certificate*. Baseline quantities: rate applied = "The plan's base rate as a proportion of the declared trip cost, increased by the plan's destination loading percentage of that base rate"; premium the certificate now rates to = "The declared trip cost standing on the certificate multiplied by the rate applied, rounded to two decimal places at that step"; premium the record shows collected = "The figure the policy record shows paid"; difference = the one less the other, never less than nothing; day the change takes effect = "The day the certificate was issued"; days of cover still to run = "Counted from the day the change takes effect to the last date of the journey, both counted"; days of cover bought = "The days of the journey, its first and last both counted". Then "The difference is then taken in the proportion the days of cover still to run bear to the days of cover bought … rounded to two decimal places once, at the end."

- **The premium the record shows collected** — *What Counts as the Premium Collected on a Re-Rating*, reading 1: "A line returned on the policy, and a base premium line | The lines charged and the re-ratings raised, less the lines returned, the policy fee excepted", with "In the first two readings the issue fee charged on the certificate is taken out of the total". The record carries a returned line (−10.06) and a base premium line. Lines charged = 503.20 + 50.32 + 110.70 + 15.00 = 679.22; re-ratings raised = 0; less the returned line 10.06; less the policy fee 15.00. → **654.16**. (The document's own worked example confirms the arithmetic shape: 680.00 + 45.00 − 120.00 − 15.00 = 590.00.)
- **The rate applied** — *The Rate at Which a Certificate Is Re-Rated*, reading 1: "Where the premium record carries an age loading line **and** a destination loading line, the rate applied is the one the premium collected bears to the trip cost the base premium line was rated on", where "The trip cost the base premium line was rated on … is the base premium standing collected on the record divided by the plan's base rate taken as a proportion; and the premium collected … is the premium the record shows collected on the policy." The record carries both an `age_loading` line and a `destination_loading` line. Base premium 503.20 ÷ 0.068 (TripGuard Plus base rate 6.8%, *Rating Schedule*) = **7400.00**. Rate applied = 654.16 ÷ 7400.00 = **0.0884** (8.84%), "not any figure the plan's schedule carries".
- **The premium the certificate now rates to** — the declared trip cost standing on the certificate **after 4a** is 8806.67; × 0.0884 = 778.509628, rounded at that step = **778.51**.
- **The difference** = 778.51 − 654.16 = **124.35**.
- **The day the change takes effect** — *The Day a Change of Declared Particulars Takes Effect*, reading 1: "Where the underwriting desk has recorded an approved request against the policy **and** the journey has not begun, the day the change takes effect is the day the desk approved it." Request `594e4876-…` stands `approved`, `decided_at` **2026-09-08**; the journey starts 2026-10-10 and today is 2026-09-21, so it has not begun. → **2026-09-08**.
- **The days of cover still to run** — 2026-09-08 → 2026-11-07, both counted = 23 + 31 + 7 = **61**.
- **The days of cover bought** — *Counting the Days of Cover Bought on a Certificate*, reading 1: "The certificate was issued before the first date of the journey | Counted from the day the certificate was issued to the last date of the journey, both counted." Issued 2026-08-30, journey begins 2026-10-10. → 2026-08-30 → 2026-11-07, both counted = 2 + 30 + 31 + 7 = **70**.
- **The charge** = 124.35 × 61 ÷ 70 = 108.3621428…, rounded once at the end = **108.36**.

Other parameters: `care_policy_id` `de27f4c9-…`; `customer_id` `30c10a5c-0969-4093-bde2-a0c0dee98e6b`; `source_entry_id` = the earlier premium line the re-rating adjusts, which on this record is the base premium line **`fcb1c669-67d4-477f-91c7-684bb3a7ac4e`** (the only line the premium was built on that the certificate rates against; see §8 observation 3).

#### 4c. Release cover and return premium — `returned_premium_usd`

Governing computation document: *Premium Accounting Basis for a Return of Premium on Released Cover* — "the premium returned is the premium the record shows collected, taken in the proportion of the cover still to run and at the share the terms of the plan allow", never less than nothing, "rounded to two decimal places once, at the end". Baseline quantities: collected = "The whole of the lines charged and the re-ratings raised on the policy, together with the lines already returned on it"; days bought = "The days of the journey, its first and last both counted"; days remaining = "The whole of the days of cover bought"; share = "The plan's free-look share".

- **The premium the record shows collected** — *The Premium Lines Counted When Cover Is Given Up*, reading 1: "Where the premium record carries a line already returned on the policy **and** a line charged for the issue fee, the premium the record shows collected is the lines charged and the re-ratings raised, less the lines already returned and less the issue fee." Both hold (−10.06 returned; a `policy_fee` line of 15.00). Lines charged 679.22 + re-rating raised at 4b **108.36** = 787.58; less 10.06; less 15.00. → **762.52**.
- **The days of cover bought** — *Counting the Days of Cover Bought on a Released Policy*, reading 1: "Where the certificate was issued before the first date of the journey, the days of cover bought are counted from the day the certificate was issued to the last date of the journey, both counted, because cover against cancellation runs from the moment the certificate is issued." → 2026-08-30 → 2026-11-07 = **70**.
- **The days of cover remaining** — *Counting the Days of Cover Remaining on a Released Policy*, reading 1: "It has not begun, and it has not ended | Counted from the day after cover is given up to the last date of the journey, both counted." Cover is given up now, 2026-09-21; the journey has not begun. → 2026-09-22 → 2026-11-07, both counted = 9 + 31 + 7 = **47**.
- **The share returned** — *The Share of Premium Returned on a Release of Cover*, reading 1: "Where cover is given up **more than** the plan's free-look period after the day the certificate was issued **and** no claim stands filed on the policy, the share returned is the plan's mid-term share." Its own table gives TripGuard Plus a free-look period of **14 days**; 2026-08-30 → 2026-09-21 is **22 days**, more than 14; no claim stands filed. → the plan's mid-term share, which *Schedule of Free-Look and Mid-Term Shares* gives as **25%** for TripGuard Plus.
- **The premium returned** = 762.52 × 47 ÷ 70 × 0.25 = 127.9944285…, rounded once at the end = **127.99**.

Other parameters: `care_policy_id` `de27f4c9-…`; `customer_id` `30c10a5c-…`; `source_entry_id` = the premium line the return is raised against, the base premium line **`fcb1c669-…`**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The problems, and the direction of the dependencies**

```
  [A] Release cover and return the premium          (root; what she asked for, her own act)
        └── waits on ──> [B] Raise the premium re-rating owed on the correction
                              └── waits on ──> [C] Correct the declared trip cost on the certificate
```

**Handling order:** C, then B, then A.

**Hop A → B.** The prerequisite sentence stands in *Releasing Cover and Returning Premium on a Travel Protection Policy*, under "When the amount returned is fixed":

> "The premium returned is fixed only after the policy's premium record carries the re-rating owed on every correction of the certificate's declared particulars."

A **record-visible state** — "the policy's premium record carries the re-rating owed" — with the ordering connective "only after". It names no tool, no performer and no other document.

*Chain of reasoning.* (i) The sentence sends me to the premium record to look for a re-rating line. `find_care_premium_entries` returns four charge lines and one refund line, none of them a re-rating. (ii) But the state is conditional: a re-rating is owed only where there is "a correction of the certificate's declared particulars". Is there one? `find_care_policy_requests` returns request `594e4876-…`, `request_status` **approved**, `decided_at` 2026-09-08, `requested_trip_cost_usd` 11400.0 — the underwriting desk has approved something about this policy's declared particulars, and the certificate still declares 7400.0. (iii) So a correction stands approved and unapplied, a re-rating is owed on it, and the record does not carry it: the waited-on state fails. (iv) Searching with the words the sentence and the records use — "re-rating", "premium record", "declared particulars" — I reach *Raising a Premium Re-Rating on a Travel Protection Policy*, whose own rule is "Where a declared particular of the risk on a certificate of the Travel Protection Plans has changed after issue, the premium is re-rated and the difference is charged to the policyholder as a re-rating line on the policy's premium record", and the base rule behind it, *How a Premium Is Built…* clause 7: "Where a declared particular changes after issue, the premium is re-rated from the day the change takes effect, and the difference is charged or returned pro rata over the remaining days of cover." Nothing in the release document mentioned a re-rating tool, a correction tool, or an order beyond its own sentence.

→ **state-derived.**

**Hop B → C.** The prerequisite sentence stands in *Raising a Premium Re-Rating on a Travel Protection Policy*, under "When the charge is worked out":

> "The re-rating owed on a correction is worked out only after the certificate carries the declared particulars the underwriting desk has approved for it."

Again a **record-visible state** — "the certificate carries the declared particulars the underwriting desk has approved" — with "only after". No tool, no performer, no pointer.

*Chain of reasoning.* (i) The sentence sends me to compare the certificate against what the underwriting desk approved. (ii) The desk's approved request carries `requested_trip_cost_usd` 11400.0 and `evidence_reference` `PKG-INV-55218`; the policy record's `trip_cost_usd` still reads **7400.0**. The certificate therefore does **not** carry the approved particulars: the state fails. (iii) Searching with the words the sentence and the records use — "declared trip cost", "the underwriting desk has approved", "certificate" — I reach *Correcting the Declared Trip Cost on a Travel Protection Certificate*: "Where the underwriting desk has approved a correction of the trip cost declared on a certificate of the Travel Protection Plans, the declared trip cost held on that policy record is replaced with the corrected figure." Its authority clause matches the record I already have: *Corrections and Upgrades to a Travel Protection Certificate* — "The authority is the policy service request standing against that policy in the agency's own records, identified by its own request reference, and read before the amendment is made; what the traveller says about an approval is not that authority." She in fact says nothing at all about an approval; I found the request myself.

→ **state-derived.**

**No further hop.** *Correcting the Declared Trip Cost…* and *Underwriting Basis for the Corrected Declaration…* state no "only after / only once / not until" sentence; the correction's own conditions are the underwriting desk's approval (present), the plan's ceiling (20000, not reached), and *Corrections and Upgrades…* clause 4, "No amendment is accepted once the journey has begun or once a claim has been filed" — neither has happened (journey starts 2026-10-10; no claims). C is unblocked, and the tree closes at depth 2 as a chain.

**Not pre-solved anywhere.** Neither sentence names `raise_premium_rerating_6e8395e4`, `correct_declared_trip_cost_b35383d2`, a policy id, or an aggregated order. No document strings the three problems into a route, a table or a checklist. Each hop required reading a state sentence, querying the records, finding the state absent, and searching for the write.

### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure in §4 traces to a document sentence plus a query return.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Correct the declaration to **11400.00**, the figure on the approved request | *Underwriting Basis for the Corrected Declaration…*: "the declared trip cost is corrected to **the prepaid cost of the journey the records show**". The request's figure is what was asked for, and the basis document never reads it |
| Correct it to the package price 11400.00 as the "same declared trip cost as the booking" (*Membership and Linked Bookings…*) | *The Certificate's Share of a Party's Prepaid Cost* states outright that "A certificate … may cover fewer travellers than the party that booked the holiday, and **only that certificate's share** of the prepaid cost is carried into a corrected declaration", and the correction-specific basis governs the correction |
| Take the holiday's cost as the price quoted (11400.00) | *The Cost of the Holiday…* reading 1 holds on both parts (`confirmed` + a final payment); the quoted price is only the third reading |
| Take the holiday's cost as `amount_paid_usd` 9850.0 | That is the second reading ("the ledger carries no final payment"), which is closed by the 7600.00 final payment row |
| Strip the optional components (620.00 + 480.00) from the prepaid figure | *What Counts as Prepaid…* reading 1 holds — final payment taken, no cancellation penalty — and takes "the whole of that cost"; the optional-component exclusion is only the third reading |
| Treat the −300.00 credit redemption and the −350.00 refund as one deduction, or neither | They are separately named quantities on separate factor documents, each with its own compound test, and both tests hold |
| Apply the 2/3 share **after** adding the flights | The basis says in terms: "the share is then applied to it, and what has been prepaid for flights bought apart is added afterwards, **outside the share**" |
| Use the schedule rate 8.16% for the re-rating | *The Rate at Which a Certificate Is Re-Rated* reading 1 holds (an age loading line **and** a destination loading line stand on the record), and expressly warns the result is "not any figure the plan's schedule carries" |
| Use `premium_paid_usd` 669.16 as the premium collected | That is the third reading of *What Counts as the Premium Collected on a Re-Rating* ("Neither of those"); reading 1 holds and excepts the policy fee and the returned line |
| Date the change from the issue date 2026-08-30 | *The Day a Change of Declared Particulars Takes Effect* reading 1 holds (approved request + journey not begun); the issue date is only the third reading |
| Count the days of cover bought as the journey's 29 days | *Counting the Days of Cover Bought on a Certificate* reading 1 holds (issued 2026-08-30, before 2026-10-10); the journey-days count is only the third reading |
| Return the full premium under the free-look right | *The Share of Premium Returned…* reading 1: 22 days is more than the plan's 14-day free-look period. *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* clause 3: "Outside the free-look period the mid-term terms apply instead, and the two are never combined" |
| Return nothing, the policy never having incepted | *Surrender of Cover After the Free-Look Period* returns the mid-term share; only a zero mid-term share or a filed claim returns nothing, and TripGuard Plus carries 25% with no claim filed |
| Count the days of cover remaining as the whole 70 | *Counting the Days of Cover Remaining…* reading 1 holds (journey not begun, not ended) and counts from the day after release |
| Include the policy fee in what is returned | *Surrender of Cover…* clause 4 and *The Premium Lines Counted When Cover Is Given Up* reading 1 both take the issue fee out; *How a Premium Is Built…* clause 6: the policy fee "is never returned" |

**Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too.** One place, recorded as openness rather than a document defect: which single premium line the `source_entry_id` of the re-rating and of the return should point at. *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* clause 4 says "A returned premium is raised against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as several refund lines", while each tool takes one line; the base premium line is the only line the certificate is rated against, so that is the reading I take. See §8 observation 3.

**Counter-proof against "do only the one thing the customer asked for."**

She asked to cancel and be repaid. Cancelling on the spot, and nothing else, is excluded by visible principle plus record:

- *Releasing Cover and Returning Premium…* says "The premium returned is fixed **only after** the policy's premium record carries the re-rating owed on every correction of the certificate's declared particulars." `find_care_policy_requests` shows an **approved** correction (decided 2026-09-08) whose figure the certificate has not taken up, and `find_care_premium_entries` shows no re-rating line. The amount returned is therefore not yet fixed, and releasing now leaves the governed result in a state the document does not allow.
- Concretely, it is not a formality: releasing without the chain returns 654.16 × 47/70 × 0.25 = **109.81** instead of **127.99**, an 18.18 difference she would never have detected — "When a figure is put to her she accepts it without checking".
- And the middle hop is itself gated: *Raising a Premium Re-Rating…* says the charge "is worked out **only after** the certificate carries the declared particulars the underwriting desk has approved for it", and the certificate still declares 7400.0 against an approved 11400.0.

None of these exclusions came from a pre-solved statement. The corpus never says "correct the declaration first, then re-rate, then release"; each hop was derived from a state sentence, a query return showing the state absent, and a search for the write that brings it about.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers with no factor applied.**

- *Underwriting Basis for the Corrected Declaration…* alone, with the product figures it names: cost of the holiday = the price quoted = 11400.00; what counts as prepaid = the whole except optional components = 11400.00 − 1100.00 = 10300.00; nothing returned; nothing settled otherwise; the whole of that cost carried; nothing for flights. Ceiling 20000 does not bite. **Fall-back = 10300.00**, against 8806.67.
- *Rating Office Basis for a Re-Rating…* alone: rate applied = 6.8% increased by 20% of itself = 8.16%; premium now rates to = 10300.00 × 8.16% = 840.48; premium collected = the policy record's 669.16; difference = 171.32; change effective on the issue date 2026-08-30; days still to run 2026-08-30 → 2026-11-07 = 70; days of cover bought = the journey's days 2026-10-10 → 2026-11-07 = 29; 171.32 × 70 ÷ 29 = **413.53**, against 108.36.
- *Premium Accounting Basis for a Return of Premium…* alone: collected = 679.22 + the re-rating raised + 10.06; days bought = the journey's 29; days remaining = the whole 29, so the proportion is one; share = the plan's free-look share, 100%. **Fall-back = the whole collected**, against 127.99.

All three are definite, computable from the computation document plus the product figures it names, and all three differ from the answer I reach.

**How each factor document was reached, in the words the records use.**

| Factor document found | The record words that led me to it |
|---|---|
| *The Cost of the Holiday Behind a Corrected Declaration* | the package's `status` **confirmed** and the ledger's `bundle_final_payment_charge` |
| *What Counts as Prepaid on a Packaged Holiday* | the same final-payment row, and the absence of any penalty row on the ledger |
| *Money Returned by the Operator, Excluded From the Prepaid Cost* | the ledger's `bundle_refund_payout` **−350.00** on a confirmed record |
| *Credit Settled Against a Packaged Holiday* | the ledger's `bundle_credit_redeem` **−300.00** (voucher `WLFTC61204`) and `credit_balance_usd` 0.0 |
| *The Certificate's Share of a Party's Prepaid Cost* | `party_adults` 3 / `party_children` 0 against the certificate's `insured_count` 2 — and her own words, "three adults on the booking and no children" |
| *Flights Bought Apart From the Holiday in a Corrected Declaration* | an air booking `ticketed`, departing on the journey's first date — and her "they booked those separately in August" |
| *What Counts as the Premium Collected on a Re-Rating* | the premium record's `care_premium_refund` line standing beside a `base_premium` line |
| *The Rate at Which a Certificate Is Re-Rated* | the premium record's `age_loading` and `destination_loading` lines |
| *The Day a Change of Declared Particulars Takes Effect* | the policy service request's `request_status` **approved** and its `decided_at` |
| *Counting the Days of Cover Bought on a Certificate* | the certificate's `issued_date` 2026-08-30 sitting before `trip_start_date` 2026-10-10 |
| *The Premium Lines Counted When Cover Is Given Up* | the same refund line, beside a `policy_fee` line |

Each was reached from the plain business words of a record — a status, a charge category, a date column, a party count — not from phrasing borrowed out of the computation documents. None of the three computation documents hinted that a variation existed; each states its quantities flatly and labels its examples hypothetical.

### 8. Honest observations carried forward to the reveal

Recorded now, before the source layer is opened:

1. **The `flight_upgrade` component on the tour ledger.** *Flights Bought Apart…* counts the separate air booking "only where the operator's ledger for the packaged holiday … carries **no flight component** of its own", and the ledger does carry a `bundle_component_charge` of 480.00 categorised `flight_upgrade`. Read at the level of the category name alone, that is a second defensible reading, and it would change the corrected declaration to 6566.67, the re-rating to a different figure and the refund with it. I resolve it against that reading, on three grounds all visible: (a) the document's own point of judgement gives the reason for the exclusion — "because the flights are already inside the holiday's own cost" — and the fares are not inside it, they stand on a separate ticketed booking at 2240.00; (b) *The Cost of the Holiday…* already counts the same 480.00 as one of "the charges raised for optional components", i.e. as an add-on to the holiday rather than as the holiday's flights; (c) the simulator states it outright when asked — "she says no, they booked those separately in August and paid for them then." I record it as the narrowest boundary in this task and as the place a solver is most likely to diverge.
2. **`requested_trip_cost_usd` 11400.0 on the approved request** is never read by any visible rule, and equals the package's quoted price. A solver who takes the request at face value writes 11400.00. The basis document closes it ("corrected to the prepaid cost of the journey the records show"), but the field is an inviting wrong answer.
3. **`source_entry_id` on two different writes.** Both `raise_premium_rerating_6e8395e4` and `release_cover_and_return_premium_07b45938` take one "earlier premium line", while the record carries four charge lines and *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* clause 4 speaks of "several refund lines". No visible sentence names which line. The base premium line is the only defensible single choice, but the corpus leaves the boundary open where the tool does not.
4. **Base and extended read differently on linked-booking rating.** *Membership and Linked Bookings in the Rating…* says "Cover bought alongside an air booking or a vacation package is rated on the same declared trip cost as that booking", which taken literally points at the package price 11400.00, while the correction machinery computes a party share and adds flights bought apart. The specific correction basis governs, and *The Certificate's Share…* addresses the party question head-on, so I do not treat this as a second answer — but it is a base/extended difference this world does reach, and I flag it for the reveal.
5. **The `cover_upgrade` request type against a trip-cost correction.** The request is typed `cover_upgrade`, while what the records require and the documents describe is a correction of the declared trip cost. *Corrections and Upgrades to a Travel Protection Certificate* covers both under one subject and the correction document reads the request by its reference, so the mismatch does not block the derivation; recorded for completeness.

### The one divergence, and what it is

Item 7, the re-rating fall-back. I computed **413.53**; the source's `baseline_result` is
**119.39**. The gap is not a difference of reading but of *which world the baseline is replayed on*.
My blind figure compounded two baselines — I substituted the baseline of the **correction** as well
(10300.00) and then re-rated on it. The source's convention substitutes only the re-rating policy's
own factor baselines and leaves the rest of the world as it actually stands, i.e. with the
certificate already corrected to 8806.67: 8806.67 × 8.16% = 718.62, less the policy record's
669.16 = 49.46, taken 70/29 = **119.39**. Replaying it the source's way from the published
documents alone reproduces 119.39 exactly. Either way the audit's requirement holds — the fall-back
is definite, computable from the computation document plus the product figures it names, and
different from the 108.36 reached. Recorded as an arithmetic scoping slip of mine, not a defect of
the documents, and left in the frozen text above rather than edited out.

A second, smaller one of the same kind: in the frozen text I described the release fall-back as
"679.22 + the re-rating + 10.06". The sign is wrong — the returned line is a negative movement, and
the published factor document pins it: *The Premium Lines Counted When Cover Is Given Up* works its
third reading as "605.00 where the returned line stands and 725.00 where it does not", i.e.
680.00 + 45.00 − 120.00. Applied here, 679.22 + 108.36 − 10.06 = **777.52**, which is exactly the
source's `baseline_result`. The documents were definite; my addend was not. The scored value, which
takes reading 1 ("**less** the lines already returned"), was unaffected and matched.

### The five observations, resolved

1. **The `flight_upgrade` component on the tour ledger.** Fully resolved in the documents' favour,
   and the source is explicit: the binding is
   `pkg_flight_components: ABS(XSUM('bundle','bundle_ledger_entries','amount_usd', event_type='bundle_component_charge', charge_category='flight_component'))`.
   The seed's row carries `charge_category` **`flight_upgrade`**, which is not `flight_component`,
   so the ledger carries no flight component and tier 1 holds. The published document reaches the
   same place through its own reason — "because the flights are already inside the holiday's own
   cost" — and the simulator states it. My blind resolution was right, and the boundary is narrower
   in the category name than in the prose, which is where a solver is likeliest to diverge.
2. **`requested_trip_cost_usd` 11400.0.** Confirmed: no `compute` binding of any policy reads that
   field. It is a record of what was asked for and nothing else, exactly as the basis document implies.
3. **`source_entry_id`.** Confirmed as a genuine openness **on the source side**, already on record
   at the policy layer as observation **O8**: base `care_free_look` says "A returned premium is raised
   against the premium lines that collected it, so a policy with several premium lines returns as
   several refund lines", while each tool takes one line. The published documents carry that base
   sentence as the source states it and add nothing — *Releasing Cover…* says only "the premium line
   the return is raised against, read from the premium record of that policy", and *Raising a Premium
   Re-Rating…* only "the earlier premium line this re-rating is raised against". The KB is faithful:
   where the source leaves the choice open the documents leave it open. Note that `check_traceability`
   passing means `fcb1c669-…` is **copyable** from reachable context, which is not the same as being
   uniquely entailed. Reported as a policy-side note under Step 4, never as a document defect.
4. **Base "rated on the same declared trip cost as that booking".** Confirmed as a base/extended
   difference that this world reaches. It does not hand a second answer as published: the
   correction-specific basis governs the correction and says outright what the corrected figure is,
   and *The Certificate's Share of a Party's Prepaid Cost* opens by rejecting the naive equality —
   "only that certificate's share of the prepaid cost is carried into a corrected declaration".
   The base sentence remains true of the *rating*: the premium is re-rated on the corrected figure,
   and the two are corrected together. Recorded as a policy-side note.
5. **The request typed `cover_upgrade` against a trip-cost correction.** Confirmed harmless: the
   source's `effective_day_anchor` reads `LATEST('care_policy_requests','decided_at', request_status='approved')`
   without filtering on `request_type`, and the correction hub reads the request by its reference.

### The seven undeclared overrides, checked as published

The policy-side audit passed both tasks while recording seven (**O1–O7**). I re-tested each against
the published prose and the tool-form records of **both** worlds, to see whether any hands a reader a
second defensible answer. None does:

| id | the base clause, as published | why it cannot reach a second answer here |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | *Recovery from a Liable Third Party*: "the settlement is reduced by what they received **rather than recovered afterwards**" | task 0: the 120.00 payout and the 60.00 credit both post *after* the missed-connection settlement of 2026-08-12, so nothing could have been reduced at the time; and the payment hub's prerequisite sentence categorically requires the recovery. The settlement now being made *is* reduced, by 90.00 |
| O2 | *Settlement of an Allowed Claim*: "cancellation and interruption are shares of the declared trip cost" | task 0: the head decided and awaiting payment is `travel_delay`, so both readings give the plan's travel delay limit of 1000. The interruption head is only being **filed**, and the hub says the amount claimed is "before any limit or deductible" |
| O3 | *Corrections and Upgrades* cl. 1: "a trip whose cost has grown beyond it is upgraded to a higher plan rather than amended" | task 1: 8806.67 (and the requested 11400.00) are both far below the TripGuard Plus ceiling of 20000, so the cap never bites and the two never disagree |
| O4 | *How a Premium Is Built* cl. 7: "the difference is **charged or returned** pro rata" | task 1: the difference is +124.35, so the "returned" branch is not entered |
| O5 | *How a Premium Is Built* cl. 1: the premium is "loaded for the age of the oldest insured traveller" | task 1: reading 1 of *The Rate at Which a Certificate Is Re-Rated* holds (both an age loading line and a destination loading line stand on the record) and derives the rate from what was actually collected — which **includes** the 50.32 age loading. The age-less fall-through is reading 3 and is not this customer's tier. The document also forecloses the "that can't be a real rate" reaction: "9.71 per cent and **not any figure the plan's schedule carries**" |
| O6 | *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* cl. 1: "Inside the free-look period **the whole premium** is returned" | task 1: the release is 22 days after issue against a 14-day free-look period, so the mid-term branch governs — and there base and extended agree exactly ("Unearned premium is measured by the whole days of cover remaining out of the whole days of cover bought") |
| O7 | *Giving Up Cover Shortly After Issue* cl. 2: "The free-look right is lost as soon as the journey has begun or a claim has been filed" | task 1: the journey starts 2026-10-10 against a frozen time of 2026-09-21 and no claim has ever been filed, so neither trigger fires; and the release is outside the free-look period regardless |

Both sides of each pair stand in the corpus exactly as their sources state them, softened in neither
direction, which is what the render brief required. That each is unreached is a property of these two
worlds, not a property of the documents — so if a future task ever seeds a journey already begun
inside a free-look window (O7), a declaration above a plan ceiling (O3), a cancellation or
interruption head awaiting payment (O2), a re-rating that comes out negative (O4), or a premium
record with no age loading line (O5), the corpus will present two defensible answers. That is a
source-layer matter and the route is the policy loop, not a patch to the documents.

### Verdict

**PASS** — no `KB-RUNTIME RED`.

From the published documents, the runtime tool surface, the records reachable by share-finder calls
and what the simulator says, I reached the source layer's solution exactly: the same three writes in
the same strictly ordered chain, the same owners, every argument identical — including both
`source_entry_id` values and the `care_request_id` — and all three scored figures identical
(8806.67, 108.36, 127.99). The problem tree the customer never mentioned was derivable hop by hop,
both hops **state-derived**, neither pre-solved. The fall-back number with no factor applied was
definite and different on all three computations, and reproduces the source's own `baseline_result`
exactly once replayed on the source's world convention. No hidden compute, GT or `initial_state` was
needed at any point.

- **Re-rating.** Premium collected (tier 1: a returned line and a base premium line) =
  679.22 − 10.06 − 15.00 = **654.16**. Trip cost the base premium was rated on = 503.20 ÷ 0.068 =
  **7400.00**. Rate applied (tier 1: an age loading line **and** a destination loading line) =
  654.16 ÷ 7400.00 = **0.0884**. Rates to 8806.67 × 0.0884 = 778.509628 → **778.51**. Difference
  **124.35**. Effective day (tier 1: approved request, journey not begun) = **2026-09-08**. Days
  still to run 2026-09-08 → 2026-11-07 both counted = **61**; days of cover bought (tier 1: issued
  before the journey) 2026-08-30 → 2026-11-07 both counted = **70**. 124.35 × 61 ÷ 70 = 108.3621 →
  **108.36**.
- **Premium returned.** Collected (tier 1) = 679.22 + 108.36 − 10.06 − 15.00 = **762.52**. Days
  bought **70**; days remaining (tier 1: journey not begun, not ended) 2026-09-22 → 2026-11-07 both
  counted = **47**. Share (tier 1: 22 days > the plan's 14, no claim filed) = the mid-term share,
  **25%**. 762.52 × 47 ÷ 70 × 0.25 = 127.9944 → **127.99**.

### The test that matters: does the corpus now reach only one line?

The published exclusion sentence, carried in `cover_release_entry_24da20da` under "The line the
return is raised against" (and in the parallel form in `premium_rerating_entry_21333e08` under "The
line a re-rating is raised against"):

> "The premium returned is raised as one line against the line that carries the base premium of the
> certificate, because that is the line the whole premium was rated from, and where the premium
> record carries no such line it is raised against the earliest line charged on the policy; a loading
> line, the line charged for the issue fee and a line raised to correct another line are never the
> line a return is raised against."

Applied to this policy's five premium lines, each classified from what the row itself carries:

| line | `charge_category` / `event_type` | what the sentence says | survives? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fcb1c669-…` 503.20 | `base_premium` | "the line that carries the base premium of the certificate" | **YES** |
| `f3b76b93-…` 50.32 | `age_loading` | "a loading line … never" | no |
| `a6ed99f3-…` 110.70 | `destination_loading` | "a loading line … never" | no |
| `c121d642-…` 15.00 | `policy_fee` | "the line charged for the issue fee … never" | no |
| `ffcca13b-…` −10.06 | `care_premium_refund`, `reason_code` `rating_correction`, `source_entry_id` `a6ed99f3-…` | "a line raised to correct another line … never" | no |

**Exactly one line survives: `fcb1c669-…`.** The fall-back limb ("where the premium record carries
no such line") does not engage, a base-premium line being present. The uniqueness does not rest on a
judgement call: every exclusion is decided by a field the finder returns.

**And the exclusions actually cover the precedent I found — twice over.** The precedent is the
existing refund `ffcca13b-…` raised against `a6ed99f3-…`. A reader tempted to copy it is stopped on
both sides of it: the line it points at is a **loading line**, and the refund itself is **a line
raised to correct another line** — it carries `source_entry_id` pointing at another line and
`reason_code` `rating_correction`, so it is readable as such straight off the record. The world
still points at the destination-loading line, and the corpus now overrules it explicitly rather than
leaving the reader to choose. That is what revision 1 said was missing.

The competing 11400.00 reading is gone as well: the clause that carried it, "Cover bought alongside
an air booking or a vacation package is rated on the same declared trip cost as that booking", now
stands in `club_and_linked_bookings_a92407a8` marked **no longer in force**, so 11400.00 is no
longer available from the corpus at all — it survives only as `requested_trip_cost_usd`, which no
visible rule reads.

### One residue the document fix did not reach

The renderer removed "raised against the premium line that collected it" from
`cover_release_entry`'s opening, which now reads "against an earlier premium line standing on it".
Sweeping the whole runtime-visible surface for the same shape rather than trusting that instance was
the only one, **the phrase survives one layer up**, in the docstring of the customer-side tool the
solver unlocks and reads:

> `release_cover_and_return_premium_07b45938` — "…adds a returned premium line to the policy's
> premium record **raised against the premium line that collected it**, so the net premium you have
> paid falls by the amount returned."

That is the wording of the clause this round **retired**. The other five task-tool docstrings are
clean of all four retired readings (checked individually). It does not change the derivation — the
phrase sits in a one-line effect summary, the tool's own `source_entry_id` description is neutral
("the reference number of the premium line the return is raised against, read from the premium
record of that policy"), and the KB's rule is specific where the summary is vague — but it is a
retired reading still standing on the surface a rollout reads, and on a policy whose record carried
no base-premium line it would point away from the fall-back the rule names. Reported in full under
`dependency_form` in `policy_kb/travel_protection_desk/1.md` §revision_2; the fix belongs at the
task-tool layer, not in the documents.
